104b3c4f orca: forward TERM/HUP through bwrap, so `orca-ide serve` stops cleanly
Review round 4. bwrap forwards no signals. Under the CLI's
--die-with-parent, a TERM to `orca-ide serve` (systemd's
KillMode=process unit, a plain kill) SIGKILLed the node supervisor
before it could stop its server; with the GUI's dieWithParent = false,
the supervisor's own signals hit the GUI's bwrap and orphaned Electron
serve, which kept the profile lock.

Both launchers -- the CLI's orca-ide and the GUI's inner orca-ide-app --
now run their bwrap in the background and forward TERM and HUP to
bwrap's one child, the sandboxed process. `<&0` and env
--default-signal=INT,QUIT undo what bash does to a background job, so
stdin and Ctrl-C behave as before. Tests: TERM reaches a node-mode
handler inside the sandbox, stdin passes through, SIGINT is not
ignored, and the CLI uses the same launcher.

Also from round 4: the die-with-parent case requires a bwrap script,
and the node-mode case compares stdout only.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Entire-Checkpoint: de6b0de03076

37db3ccb orca: the GUI outlives the `orca-ide open` that starts it
Review round 3 (Critical). wrapType2 defaults to --die-with-parent, and
every wrapper layer execs the next, so a GUI that `orca-ide open` spawns
detached is a bwrap whose parent is the CLI -- SIGKILLed the moment
`open` returns. dieWithParent = false; a test case holds the launcher
to it.

The node-mode case now checks printed output under a timeout: with the
env var lost on the way it would be a GUI launch, which a running
Orca's single-instance lock answers with exit 0. Comment fixes: AppRun's
--no-sandbox in node mode, appimageContents' users, the header's
description of Orca's own ~/.local/bin symlink. --version matches whole
words.

Not changed (nits): the test's skill list duplicates orcaSkills, so an
addition is not checked; files a skill dir has beyond its manifest are
not flagged; a failed fetch realise shows up as "missing"; README's
test list; an empty /etc/hostname skips the uname -n fallback.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Entire-Checkpoint: 61a8d5ea6654

4e0f5355 orca: keep --ozone-platform out of node mode; tests run under CI
Review round 2. `orca-ide serve` probes ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE with
ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1, and Node rejected the GUI wrapper's always-on
--ozone-platform=wayland (exit 9), silently dropping the orcad runtime.
The wrapper is hand-written now and adds the flag only outside node mode.

Tests: read /etc/hostname (what CI writes) with uname -n as the fallback
inside Orca's sandbox, in both orca tests; jq instead of python3, which
CI's tool shell lacks, hashing every file the manifest lists; hold
ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE to exactly the profile's nixGL-wrapped GUI; a node-
mode case for the probe above; tighter bwrap and guide-title matches.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Entire-Checkpoint: af092d532a0c

777a68b5 orca: `orca-ide` is the CLI, the GUI is `orca-ide-app`
Review round 1: Orca's skills tell agents outside an Orca terminal on
Linux to run `orca-ide`, never bare `orca` -- here that started the GUI.
Match upstream's Linux install instead: orca-ide and orca are the CLI,
the GUI wrapper and desktop Exec move to orca-ide-app.

ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE points `orca-ide open` at the nixGL-wrapped GUI;
without it the CLI spawns the raw Electron in its own env, which has no
wayland flag and exits on Hyprland.

The test now also holds the CLI launcher to being bwrap (run from an
Orca terminal it is already inside an FHS env, so a bare wrapper would
pass), runs `skills get` under both names, and checks the skills rev is
the app's own sourceCommit. The rev is in the fetch's store name, so a
rev bump without a hash bump fails instead of reusing the old tree.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Entire-Checkpoint: 253006912444

9e53e6cc orca: install the CLI as `orca` and six of its agent skills
The app's own installer only reaches an Orca terminal (a PATH shim there,
and a ~/.local/bin symlink to a raw store path). Run its CLI script in the
GUI's FHS env as `orca`, so it works from any shell; the skills are stubs
that call `orca skills get`, so they need it.

Skills come from stablyai/orca at e6f7fba5, the commit this AppImage was
built from; tests/orca-cli-skills.sh holds them to the sha256s in the
build's own current-manifest.json.

+# that `orca-ide` and `orca` are the CLI and run from any shell, not only an
+# Orca terminal, and that the skills in ~/.claude/skills are the bytes this
+# Orca build expects.

+# puts a shim dir on PATH there (ORCA_CLI_BIN_DIR) and symlinks
+# ~/.local/bin/orca-ide at a raw /nix/store path, a script that runs Electron

+# that tell the agent to run `orca-ide skills get <name>`, so a skill without a
+# working CLI is a dead end. And the skills are pinned to a commit separately
+# from the AppImage version; bumping one without the other silently installs
+# guides for a different CLI. Orca ships the expected hashes in
+# resources/skills/current-manifest.json, so that is what the files are held to.

+#   tests/orca-cli-skills.sh    eval + build this host's config and test it

+set -o pipefail

+# must not also claim `orca-ide` -- in the profile it would shadow one of them.

+  else fail "$b skills get" "$(printf '%s' "$got" | head -3)"; fi
+done

+# The rev is pinned by hand next to the version; the app knows its own.
+rev=$(nix eval --raw "$HM.home.file" --apply 'f: f.".claude/skills/orca-cli".source' | sed -nE 's|.*-orca-skills-([0-9a-f]{40})/.*|\1|p')

+    || { fail "$s" "no home.file .claude/skills/$s"; continue; }

+    "f: builtins.head (builtins.attrNames (builtins.getContext f.\".claude/skills/$s\".source))" 2>/dev/null)

+  else fail "$s" "${out:-$src is missing}"; fi
+done

+[ "$fails" -eq 0 ]

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Cases for the claims orca.nix makes about the Orca CLI and its agent skills:
+# that `orca-ide` and `orca` are the CLI and run from any shell, not only an
+# Orca terminal, and that the skills in ~/.claude/skills are the bytes this
+# Orca build expects.
+#
+# Why this needs a test. Orca's own installer only reaches an Orca terminal: it
+# puts a shim dir on PATH there (ORCA_CLI_BIN_DIR) and symlinks
+# ~/.local/bin/orca-ide at a raw /nix/store path, a script that runs Electron
+# against the host's libraries outside the FHS env. The skills are stubs
+# that tell the agent to run `orca-ide skills get <name>`, so a skill without a
+# working CLI is a dead end. And the skills are pinned to a commit separately
+# from the AppImage version; bumping one without the other silently installs
+# guides for a different CLI. Orca ships the expected hashes in
+# resources/skills/current-manifest.json, so that is what the files are held to.
+#
+# Usage:
+#   tests/orca-cli-skills.sh    eval + build this host's config and test it
+
+set -u
+set -o pipefail
+
+fails=0; n=0
+pass() { n=$((n+1)); echo "ok   $1"; }
+fail() { n=$((n+1)); echo "FAIL $1: $2"; fails=$((fails+1)); }
+T=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$T"' EXIT
+
+FLAKE=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)
+# /etc/hostname is what CI writes to say which host it is; Orca's sandbox does
+# not bind it in, so fall back to uname -n there.
+HM="$FLAKE#homeConfigurations.$(cat /etc/hostname 2>/dev/null || uname -n).config"
+SKILLS="orca-cli orchestration computer-use orca-per-workspace-env orca-linear linear-tickets"
+
+pkg_attr() { # pkg_attr <pname> <attr>
+  nix eval --raw "$HM.home.packages" \
+    --apply "ps: (builtins.head (builtins.filter (p: (p.pname or \"\") == \"$1\") ps)).$2"
+}
+drv=$(pkg_attr orca-cli drvPath) || { echo "no orca-cli in home.packages here" >&2; exit 1; }
+want_version=$(pkg_attr orca-cli version) && [ -n "$want_version" ] \
+  || { echo "orca-cli has no version" >&2; exit 1; }
+CLI=$(nix-store --realise "$drv" | tail -1) || { echo "could not build orca-cli" >&2; exit 1; }
+gui_drv=$(pkg_attr orca drvPath) || { echo "no orca in home.packages here" >&2; exit 1; }
+GUI=$(nix-store --realise "$gui_drv" | tail -1) || { echo "could not build orca" >&2; exit 1; }
+echo "testing $CLI and $GUI"
+
+# The skills' own rule: outside an Orca terminal, on Linux, the CLI is
+# `orca-ide`; elsewhere it is `orca`. Both names must be the CLI, and the GUI
+# must not also claim `orca-ide` -- in the profile it would shadow one of them.
+for b in orca orca-ide; do
+  if [ -x "$CLI/bin/$b" ]; then pass "orca-cli provides bin/$b"
+  else fail "bin/$b" "missing from $CLI"; fi
+done
+if [ -x "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" ] && [ ! -e "$GUI/bin/orca-ide" ]; then
+  pass "the GUI is orca-ide-app and leaves orca-ide to the CLI"
+else fail "GUI bin names" "$(ls "$GUI/bin" | paste -sd' ')"; fi
+
+# Run from an Orca terminal, this test is already inside the GUI's FHS env, so
+# a bare wrapper exec'ing the Electron binary would pass every case below.
+# Hold the launcher itself to being a bwrap one.
+cli_bwrap=$(readlink -f "$CLI/bin/.orca-ide-bwrap")
+if grep -qE '^exec "\$\{cmd\[@\]\}"|/bin/bwrap' "$cli_bwrap"; then
+  pass "the CLI runs in its own bwrap FHS env"
+else fail "CLI launcher" "$cli_bwrap does not exec bwrap"; fi
+
+# `orca open` spawns the app; without ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE that is the raw
+# Electron in the CLI's env, with no wayland flag, fonts or nixGL.
+app=$(grep -o -- '--setenv ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE [^ ]*' "$cli_bwrap" | awk '{print $3}')
+# Exactly the profile's GUI: the unwrapped one has an orca-ide-app too, minus nixGL.
+if [ "$app" = "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" ]; then
+  pass "orca open launches the profile's nixGL-wrapped GUI"
+else fail "ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE" "'${app:-unset}', want $GUI/bin/orca-ide-app"; fi
+
+# `orca-ide serve` probes that same executable in node mode, with a script as
+# argv; Node rejects --ozone-platform, so the wrapper must leave it off there.
+# Print, not exit status: if the env var were lost on the way, this would be a
+# GUI launch, which a running Orca's single-instance lock answers with 0.
+out=$(ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 timeout 60 "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" -p '"node-ok"' 2>"$T/node-err")
+if [ "$out" = node-ok ]; then
+  pass "orca-ide-app runs in node mode (serve's runtime probe)"
+else fail "orca-ide-app node mode" "${out:-$(tail -1 "$T/node-err")}"; fi
+
+# Stopping `orca-ide serve` (systemctl, its own supervisor, a plain kill)
+# signals the outermost pid. bwrap neither forwards signals nor dies when
+# --die-with-parent is off, so without a forwarding launcher the TERM kills
+# bwrap and the process inside keeps the profile lock. Node mode stands in for
+# the GUI here: same launcher, and it can report what it saw. The script exits
+# on its own after 20s, so a regression cannot leak it.
+ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" -e '
+  process.on("SIGTERM", () => { console.log("got-term"); process.exit(0); });
+  console.log("ready"); setTimeout(() => process.exit(3), 20000);' >"$T/term" 2>&1 &
+w=$!
+for _ in $(seq 150); do grep -q ready "$T/term" && break; sleep 0.2; done
+kill -TERM "$w" 2>/dev/null; wait "$w"; rc=$?
+if grep -q got-term "$T/term" && [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
+  pass "TERM to the GUI launcher reaches the process in the sandbox"
+else fail "signal forwarding" "rc=$rc, saw: $(tr '\n' ' ' < "$T/term")"; fi
+
+# The forwarding launcher backgrounds bwrap, which in a non-interactive shell
+# means stdin from /dev/null and SIGINT ignored -- the CLI reads stdin, and
+# Ctrl-C must still kill it. Run in the foreground here, so neither is the
+# test's own doing.
+got=$(echo stdin-ok | ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" -e 'process.stdin.pipe(process.stdout)' 2>&1)
+if [ "$got" = stdin-ok ]; then pass "the launcher passes stdin through"
+else fail "stdin" "got '$got'"; fi
+ign=$(ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" -p \
+  'require("fs").readFileSync("/proc/self/status","utf8").match(/SigIgn:\s*(\w+)/)[1]' 2>&1)
+if [ -n "$ign" ] && [ $(( 0x$ign & 2 )) -eq 0 ]; then pass "SIGINT is not ignored inside the launcher"
+else fail "SIGINT" "SigIgn=$ign"; fi
+
+# The CLI uses the same launcher (it is what systemctl stops for a service
+# `orca-ide serve`), wrapping its own bwrap.
+if grep -q 'forward-signals' "$CLI/bin/orca-ide" 2>/dev/null \
+   && grep -q '\.orca-ide-bwrap' "$CLI/bin/orca-ide"; then
+  pass "the CLI forwards signals into its sandbox too"
+else fail "CLI launcher" "$CLI/bin/orca-ide is not the forwarding launcher"; fi
+
+# `orca-ide open` spawns the GUI detached, but each wrapper layer execs the
+# next, so the GUI's bwrap is the CLI's direct child; with --die-with-parent
+# it is SIGKILLed the moment `open` returns.
+gui_launcher=$(readlink -f "$GUI/bin/.orca-ide-unwrapped")
+if grep -q '/bin/bwrap' "$gui_launcher" 2>/dev/null && ! grep -q -- '--die-with-parent' "$gui_launcher"; then
+  pass "the GUI outlives the orca-ide open that started it"
+else fail "GUI launcher" "$gui_launcher passes --die-with-parent (or is missing)"; fi
+
+# The manifest travels with the extracted AppImage, which the CLI's runScript
+# references, so it is in the CLI's closure.
+contents=$(nix-store -qR "$CLI" | while read -r p; do
+  [ -f "$p/resources/skills/current-manifest.json" ] && echo "$p"; done | head -1)
+[ -n "$contents" ] || { echo "no extracted AppImage in the closure of $CLI" >&2; exit 1; }
+manifest="$contents/resources/skills/current-manifest.json"
+
+# Outside an Orca terminal: none of its env, none of its shim dir on PATH.
+clean_path=$(printf '%s' "$PATH" | tr ':' '\n' | grep -v 'linux-orca-cli-shim' | paste -sd:)
+outside() { env $(compgen -e | grep '^ORCA_' | sed 's/^/-u /') PATH="$clean_path" "$@"; }
+
+got=$(outside "$CLI/bin/orca" --version 2>&1)
+if printf '%s' "$got" | grep -qwF "$want_version"; then pass "orca --version reports $want_version outside Orca"
+else fail "orca --version" "got '$got', want $want_version"; fi
+
+# What every skill stub runs, under both names the stubs choose between.
+for b in orca-ide orca; do
+  got=$(outside "$CLI/bin/$b" skills get orca-cli 2>&1)
+  if printf '%s' "$got" | grep -q '^# Orca CLI'; then pass "$b skills get orca-cli prints the guide outside Orca"
+  else fail "$b skills get" "$(printf '%s' "$got" | head -3)"; fi
+done
+
+# The rev is pinned by hand next to the version; the app knows its own.
+rev=$(nix eval --raw "$HM.home.file" --apply 'f: f.".claude/skills/orca-cli".source' | sed -nE 's|.*-orca-skills-([0-9a-f]{40})/.*|\1|p')
+if [ -n "$rev" ] && grep -aqF "sourceCommit:\`$rev\`" "$contents/resources/app.asar"; then
+  pass "skills rev ${rev:0:8} is this build's sourceCommit"
+else fail "skills rev" "'${rev:-unparsed}' is not the sourceCommit in app.asar"; fi
+
+for s in $SKILLS; do
+  src=$(nix eval --raw "$HM.home.file" --apply "f: toString f.\".claude/skills/$s\".source" 2>/dev/null) \
+    || { fail "$s" "no home.file .claude/skills/$s"; continue; }
+  # The source is a subpath of a fetch; realise the fetch's derivation itself.
+  srcdrv=$(nix eval --raw "$HM.home.file" --apply \
+    "f: builtins.head (builtins.attrNames (builtins.getContext f.\".claude/skills/$s\".source))" 2>/dev/null)
+  nix-store --realise "$srcdrv" >/dev/null
+  # Every file the manifest lists for the skill, as "<sha256>  <path>" lines.
+  want=$(jq -r --arg n "$s" '.skills[] | select(.name == $n) | .files[] | "\(.exactSha256)  \(.path)"' "$manifest")
+  [ -n "$want" ] || { fail "$s" "no entry in the manifest"; continue; }
+  if out=$(cd "$src" 2>/dev/null && printf '%s\n' "$want" | sha256sum --quiet -c - 2>&1); then
+    pass "$s matches this build's manifest ($(printf '%s\n' "$want" | wc -l) files)"
+  else fail "$s" "${out:-$src is missing}"; fi
+done
+
+printf '\n%d/%d passed\n' "$((n-fails))" "$n"
+[ "$fails" -eq 0 ]

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -e

THIS="$0"
# http://stackoverflow.com/questions/3190818/
args=("$@")
NUMBER_OF_ARGS="$#"

if [ -z "$APPDIR" ] ; then
  # Find the AppDir. It is the directory that contains AppRun.
  # This assumes that this script resides inside the AppDir or a subdirectory.
  # If this script is run inside an AppImage, then the AppImage runtime likely has already set $APPDIR
  path="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "${THIS}")")"
  while [[ "$path" != "" && ! -e "$path/AppRun" ]]; do
    path=${path%/*}
  done
  APPDIR="$path"
fi

if [ -z "$APPDIR" ] ; then
  echo "ERROR: could not locate the AppDir. Ensure this script is run from within a properly structured AppImage." >&2
  exit 1
fi

export PATH="${APPDIR}:${APPDIR}/usr/sbin${PATH:+:${PATH}}"
export XDG_DATA_DIRS="${APPDIR}/usr/share/${XDG_DATA_DIRS:+:${XDG_DATA_DIRS}}:/usr/share/gnome:/usr/local/share/:/usr/share/"
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="${APPDIR}/usr/lib${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:+:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH}}"
export GSETTINGS_SCHEMA_DIR="${APPDIR}/usr/share/glib-2.0/schemas${GSETTINGS_SCHEMA_DIR:+:${GSETTINGS_SCHEMA_DIR}}"

BIN="$APPDIR/orca-ide"

if [ -z "$APPIMAGE_EXIT_AFTER_INSTALL" ] ; then
  trap atexit EXIT
fi

isEulaAccepted=1

HAVE_NO_SANDBOX=0
for arg in "${args[@]}" ; do
  if [ "$arg" = --no-sandbox ] ; then
    HAVE_NO_SANDBOX=1
    break
  fi
done
NO_SANDBOX=()
# Use 'unshare -Ur true' as a heuristic to detect whether user namespaces are available.
# Notes:
#   - When running as root, this check will always succeed even if the sandbox configuration
#     actually relies on unprivileged user namespaces. In practice, Chrome/Electron usually
#     disables or adjusts the sandbox separately when running as root, so this probe is mostly
#     a no-op in that scenario.
#   - On minimal systems (e.g. Alpine or stripped-down containers) 'unshare' may not exist.
#     In that case the shell will return exit code 127 ("command not found"), which will cause
#     us to add '--no-sandbox'. This is an intentional fail-safe: we prefer the app to start
#     without sandboxing rather than crash on startup.
if [ $HAVE_NO_SANDBOX -eq 0 ] && ! unshare -Ur true 2>/dev/null ; then
  NO_SANDBOX=(--no-sandbox)
fi

atexit()
{
  if [ $isEulaAccepted == 1 ] ; then
    if [ $NUMBER_OF_ARGS -eq 0 ] ; then
      exec "$BIN" "${NO_SANDBOX[@]}"
    else
      exec "$BIN" "${NO_SANDBOX[@]}" "${args[@]}"
    fi
  fi
}

error()
{
  if [ -x /usr/bin/zenity ] ; then
    LD_LIBRARY_PATH="" zenity --error --text "${1}" 2>/dev/null
  elif [ -x /usr/bin/kdialog ] ; then
    LD_LIBRARY_PATH="" kdialog --msgbox "${1}" 2>/dev/null
  elif [ -x /usr/bin/Xdialog ] ; then
    LD_LIBRARY_PATH="" Xdialog --msgbox "${1}" 2>/dev/null
  else
    echo "${1}"
  fi
  exit 1
}

yesno()
{

  elif [ -x /usr/bin/kdialog ] ; then
    LD_LIBRARY_PATH="" kdialog --title "$TITLE" --yesno "$TEXT" || exit 0

# `-f` rejects a same-named directory that `-x` alone would accept.

set -e

args=("$@")

if [ -z "$APPDIR" ] ; then
  # Find the AppDir. It is the directory that contains AppRun.
  # This assumes that this script resides inside the AppDir or a subdirectory.
  # If this script is run inside an AppImage, then the AppImage runtime likely has already set $APPDIR
  path="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "${THIS}")")"
  while [[ "$path" != "" && ! -e "$path/AppRun" ]]; do

  APPDIR="$path"
fi

if [ -z "$APPDIR" ] ; then
  echo "ERROR: could not locate the AppDir. Ensure this script is run from within a properly structured AppImage." >&2
  exit 1
fi

export PATH="${APPDIR}:${APPDIR}/usr/sbin${PATH:+:${PATH}}"
export XDG_DATA_DIRS="${APPDIR}/usr/share/${XDG_DATA_DIRS:+:${XDG_DATA_DIRS}}:/usr/share/gnome:/usr/local/share/:/usr/share/"
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="${APPDIR}/usr/lib${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:+:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH}}"
export GSETTINGS_SCHEMA_DIR="${APPDIR}/usr/share/glib-2.0/schemas${GSETTINGS_SCHEMA_DIR:+:${GSETTINGS_SCHEMA_DIR}}"

BIN="$APPDIR/orca-ide"

if [ -z "$APPIMAGE_EXIT_AFTER_INSTALL" ] ; then
  trap atexit EXIT
fi

isEulaAccepted=1

HAVE_NO_SANDBOX=0
for arg in "${args[@]}" ; do
  if [ "$arg" = --no-sandbox ] ; then
    HAVE_NO_SANDBOX=1
    break
  fi
done
NO_SANDBOX=()
# Use 'unshare -Ur true' as a heuristic to detect whether user namespaces are available.
# Notes:
#   - When running as root, this check will always succeed even if the sandbox configuration
#     actually relies on unprivileged user namespaces. In practice, Chrome/Electron usually
#     disables or adjusts the sandbox separately when running as root, so this probe is mostly
#     a no-op in that scenario.
#   - On minimal systems (e.g. Alpine or stripped-down containers) 'unshare' may not exist.
#     In that case the shell will return exit code 127 ("command not found"), which will cause
#     us to add '--no-sandbox'. This is an intentional fail-safe: we prefer the app to start
#     without sandboxing rather than crash on startup.
if [ $HAVE_NO_SANDBOX -eq 0 ] && ! unshare -Ur true 2>/dev/null ; then
  NO_SANDBOX=(--no-sandbox)
fi

atexit()
{
  if [ $isEulaAccepted == 1 ] ; then
    if [ $NUMBER_OF_ARGS -eq 0 ] ; then
      exec "$BIN" "${NO_SANDBOX[@]}"
    else
      exec "$BIN" "${NO_SANDBOX[@]}" "${args[@]}"
    fi
  fi
}

    LD_LIBRARY_PATH="" zenity --error --text "${1}" 2>/dev/null

    LD_LIBRARY_PATH="" kdialog --msgbox "${1}" 2>/dev/null
  elif [ -x /usr/bin/Xdialog ] ; then
    LD_LIBRARY_PATH="" Xdialog --msgbox "${1}" 2>/dev/null
  else
    echo "${1}"
  fi
  exit 1

  elif [ -x /usr/bin/kdialog ] ; then
    LD_LIBRARY_PATH="" kdialog --title "$TITLE" --yesno "$TEXT" || exit 0
